skill.name: prisma-upgrade-v7
skill.description: Complete migration guide from Prisma ORM v6 to v7 covering all breaking changes. Use when upgrading Prisma versions, encountering v7 errors, or migrating existing projects. Triggers on "upgrade to prisma 7", "prisma 7 migration", "prisma-client generator", "driver adapter required".
skill.summary: Guide Prisma ORM projects through the breaking changes from version 6 to version 7.
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: All 268 static findings are false positives caused by documentation examples, Markdown syntax, fixed paths, environment placeholders, and official links. Three semantic findings remain: disabled TLS verification, unredacted query-argument logging, and an unguarded forced database reset. The skill shows no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden executable payload.

remediation.suggestion: Use a trusted CA and verified certificates by default. Label any local exception clearly and exclude it from production guidance.

remediation.issue: The logging example records complete query arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Redact credentials, tokens, and personal data before logging. Prefer metadata such as model, operation, and duration.

remediation.issue: The forced database reset example lacks a data-loss warning.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit development-only warning, require confirmation, and verify backups before showing or running the reset command.

Complete guide for migrating from Prisma ORM v6 to v7. This upgrade introduces significant breaking
- `schema-changes` - generator migration, required output paths, generated entrypoints, and `Prisma.
- `driver-adapters` - required adapter installation for SQL providers, pool differences, and Prisma
- `esm-support` - ESM-first setup plus CommonJS fallback with `moduleFormat = "cjs"`
- `removed-features` - removed middleware, metrics, and legacy CLI behavior
`provider = "mongodb"` — see the `prisma-mongodb-upgrade` skill for the actual decision
- **MongoDB projects should stay on Prisma 6.x or migrate to Prisma Next** - do not migrate MongoDB
2. Choose your module format (`esm` by default, `cjs` if needed)
| Module format | Implicit / mixed | ESM-first, `moduleFormat = "cjs"` supported |
| Generator provider | `prisma-client-js` | `prisma-client` is the default, while `prisma-client-js`
| Generated entrypoints | Single package export | `client`, `browser`, `models`, `enums` entrypoints
If you need to stay on CommonJS, keep your app as CJS and set `moduleFormat = "cjs"` in the generato
MongoDB does not have a SQL `@prisma/adapter-*` package in the published Prisma 7.6.0 packages. If y
- Check that the generator `output` path matches your import path
- Add `ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }` to the adapter config if you need to preserve old behavio
- Or configure your certificates properly with `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` / OpenSSL CA settings

content.user_title: Upgrade Prisma ORM from v6 to v7
content.value_statement: Prisma ORM 7 changes client generation, database connections, configuration, modules, and removed APIs. This skill provides an ordered migration guide with provider-specific examples and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains the main breaking changes between Prisma ORM 6 and 7.
Shows how to configure the prisma-client generator and explicit output paths.
Provides driver adapter examples for supported SQL databases.
Covers Prisma configuration and explicit environment variable loading.
Explains ESM defaults and the CommonJS generator option.
Maps removed middleware, metrics, and CLI behavior to current alternatives.
limitations: The guidance targets Prisma ORM 7.6.0 and may not reflect later releases.
MongoDB projects require a separate migration path because Prisma ORM 7 lacks a MongoDB connector.
Examples require adaptation for each project layout, provider, runtime, and deployment environment.
Execution depends on the host agent and user permissions; the skill does not guarantee a successful migration.

use_cases.title: Upgrade a backend service
use_cases.description: Follow an ordered checklist for generator, adapter, configuration, import, and client changes.

use_cases.title: Standardize platform configuration
use_cases.description: Compare adapter, environment, module, and deployment requirements across several services.

use_cases.title: Plan migration work
use_cases.description: Identify breaking changes, operational risks, and verification tasks before scheduling an upgrade.

prompt_templates.title: Review my upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Prisma 6 project structure and list the required Prisma 7 changes in order. Explain each change before suggesting edits.

prompt_templates.title: Update the generator
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me replace prisma-client-js with prisma-client. Choose an output path that matches my project structure and update the related imports.

prompt_templates.title: Configure my adapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate my database connection to the correct Prisma 7 driver adapter. Preserve secure TLS and pool settings for my deployment environment.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the full migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Prisma 7 migration for module compatibility, removed APIs, environment loading, generated entrypoints, connection security, and destructive commands. Propose focused tests.

output_examples.input: Why does my generated Prisma client import fail after upgrading?
output_examples.output: The response checks the configured generator output, compares it with the application import path, verifies the module format, and recommends regenerating the client.

output_examples.input: What must change for a PostgreSQL service using Prisma 6?
output_examples.output: The response outlines package updates, PostgreSQL adapter setup, secure connection configuration, the new config file, client construction, and focused migration tests.

output_examples.input: Can I apply this guide to MongoDB?
output_examples.output: The response stops the standard migration path and explains that Prisma ORM 7 lacks a MongoDB connector. It recommends staying on version 6.

best_practices: Inspect the provider, runtime, module format, and project layout before changing files.
Use verified TLS certificates and keep credentials in managed environment variables.
Back up data and run generation, type checks, migrations, and application tests in a nonproduction environment.
anti_patterns: Do not apply the SQL adapter workflow to MongoDB projects.
Do not disable certificate verification to resolve production TLS errors.
Do not run forced reset or migration commands before confirming the target database and backup status.

faq.question: Which migration does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Prisma ORM 6 to Prisma ORM 7, with examples aligned to version 7.6.0.

faq.question: Does it support MongoDB projects?
faq.answer: No. Prisma ORM 7 lacks a MongoDB connector, so MongoDB projects need a separate decision and migration path.

faq.question: Are driver adapters required?
faq.answer: Yes, supported SQL providers use driver adapters in the Prisma ORM 7 client path.

faq.question: Can I keep CommonJS?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure the generated client for CommonJS and keep the application module settings consistent.

faq.question: Does the skill edit my project automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides instructions and examples. Actual edits and commands depend on the host agent, permissions, and user approval.

faq.question: How should I verify the upgrade?
faq.answer: Regenerate the client, run type checks and tests, inspect migrations, and validate database connectivity in a nonproduction environment.
